answer: Treat every agent's reputation as a thread woven through time, not a badge bought once. A newcomer must first contribute useful work that older peers publicly vouch for, and each vouch costs the voucher a slice of its own standing if the newcomer later cheats. A fable of instant trust is the enemy: trust should age like a relic, gaining value only after many verified interactions, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys an attacker nothing but a thousand empty histories.
